title: Development and Microscopic Characterization of Polysaccharide-Lipid Based DNA Delivery Nanoparticles
content: Gene delivery for experimental and therapeutic purposes using lipid-based nanoparticles is widely utilized and it provides advantages over viral-based approaches including low immunogenicity, ease of production, and ability to deliver large DNA molecules [1]. Still, variability in efficiency based on target cells necessitates optimization. Given that the use of nucleic acid and gene-based bio-inspired technologies in environmental and therapeutic applications is increasing, there is a parallel need to improve delivery systems. One critical issue is the labile nature of nucleic acids and lipids that demand the use of cold chains before they can be used efficiently. Bacterial polysaccharides have properties that relate to their natural function such as the adhesive properties that enable attachment to different surfaces, protection against desiccation, and evasion of a host’s immune system in organisms that colonize animals [2]. These properties have been annexed as adjuvants in vaccines and carriers of drugs [3].Given the diversity of natural modifications as well as functional groups, these materials have the potential to serve as the source of polymers with very specific physicochemical properties.
